clue.text: Prosperous food shop has 100 credit notes for fruit

blocks.note: a golden period is a prosperous one
short for delicatessen
joins the parts, giving no letters
C is the Roman numeral for 100
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: A thriving grocer has a hundred notes of credit outstanding for its fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' simply means the pieces follow on from one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden Delicious is a popular variety of apple, so it is an example of fruit.

clue.text: Birds leave before buzzard's tail wags

indicators.note: a tail is the end of a creature, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: to leave is to go
the final letter of buzzard
wags and wits are both jokers

explanation.surface: Little birds make off before a buzzard's tail starts flicking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wags' looks like a verb about the tail, but it is a noun: wags are witty people.
explanation.definitionFit: Godwits are long-billed wading birds, so the plural fits the plural definition.

clue.text: In conversation, lean over composer

indicators.note: conversation is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a ship that leans over lists

explanation.surface: In a chat, someone bends towards a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer's name is said like LISTS; to list is to lean to one side, as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian Romantic composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Dish out short, hip menu for music producer

something short is lacking its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: out with its last letter dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A waiter serves a brief trendy menu to a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish out' reads as one phrase about serving food; it splits into the anagram signal and the word 'out', which is then shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphonium is a brass instrument, something that produces music.

clue.text: Daughter with half of beer eating pub meal

indicators.note: only one of the two halves of the word is kept, the rest discarded
something that eats takes another thing inside it

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
the second half of beer
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A daughter with half a pint is eating pub food.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is the main meal of the day.

clue.text: American tense visiting host's embassy

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so these letters go inside the following word

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a host and a legion are both great numbers

explanation.surface: A nervous American calls in at the host nation's embassy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A legation is a diplomatic mission ranked below an embassy, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Centre put the ball over the line with seconds to go

indicators.note: the s abbreviation for seconds is to depart from the word

blocks.clueFragment: put the ball over the line
blocks.note: getting a ball over the line scores a try or goal

explanation.surface: A centre forward bundles the ball in just before the final whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre' looks like a player's position in a football match, but it is the definition; seconds means the abbreviation S, which is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of something is its central part.

clue.text: Under the weather, turned green perhaps

blocks.note: milk that has turned has gone off
green is an example of a colour

explanation.surface: Someone feeling ill has gone green in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface links feeling sick with turning green; in the wordplay the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling off-colour and being under the weather are both idioms for being slightly unwell.

clue.text: Lecture we hear from drunk tank

indicators.note: this is how the word comes out when slurred by someone who has had too much

blocks.note: a lecture is a sermon, and a drunk slurs its S into SH

explanation.surface: A sermon delivered by someone who is very drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tank' could suggest drinking too, but here it is the definition: the American Second World War tank.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sherman was the main American battle tank of the Second World War.

clue.text: Stand up for working waste collector

indicators.note: letters that are working are put to use in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Supporting refuse workers in their job.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan collects the sweepings and rubbish brushed off a floor.

clue.text: Animal from middle of Africa falling over in slip

indicators.note: only the central letters of the word are kept
something that falls over ends up upside down, so the letters run the other way
these letters are placed inside the following word

blocks.note: the two central letters of Africa
a slip or blunder is a gaffe

explanation.surface: An animal in central Africa slips and falls over.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is the long-necked African mammal, an obvious example of an animal.

clue.text: Temperature within river not relaxing for shy person

indicators.note: something relaxing loosens up, so the letters come loose and rearrange
this letter sits inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for temperature
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cold river that never lets up is no place for a timid soul.
explanation.walkthrough: The temperature letter goes inside the rearranged letters of 'river not', after the first two.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert is a reserved, inward-looking person, so shy describes them well.

clue.text: Rush and ZZ Top, or occasionally Miles

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: A list of rock acts: Rush, ZZ Top, or perhaps Miles Davis.
explanation.walkthrough: Rush and ZZ Top are rock bands and Miles suggests the jazzman Miles Davis, so 'Rush' hides as one more musician.
explanation.definitionFit: To zoom is to move very fast, which is what rushing means.

clue.text: Very focused at first, draw snowflake

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is wanted

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
the initial letter of focused
a drawn game is a tie

explanation.surface: An artist concentrates hard at the start to sketch a snowflake.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowflake is slang for an oversensitive person, much like a softie.

clue.text: Face fell when going round part of house

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the opposite direction

blocks.note: the face of a building is its front
a fell is upland moor in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone's face dropped as they went round part of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like the past of fall, but it is a noun: a fell is a hill or moor in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The front room is the living room at the front of a house.

clue.text: Report to banks in Wisconsin's thriving area

indicators.note: the banks of something are its edges, so only its outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: a report is a loud bang, a boom
taken as written
the first and last letters of Wisconsin

explanation.surface: A report sent to the banks in a booming part of Wisconsin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests finance, but it means the edges of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom town is a settlement that grows suddenly and prospers, a thriving place.

clue.text: Not a fan of chimpanzee snack?

definitions.text: Not a fan of chimpanzee snack?

blocks.note: surface: someone who has no love for apes
setter's reading: the nut here is not an enthusiast but a food that apes are fed

explanation.walkthrough: A nut can mean a fan; the clue says this one is not a devotee of apes but a peanut in its shell, the snack often associated with them.
explanation.definitionFit: A monkey nut is a peanut in its shell, a common snack.

clue.text: Water getting into a lot of snappy running shoes

indicators.note: a lot of something is most of it but not all, so the end letter is lost
entering something means going inside it

blocks.note: snappy means terse; most of it is used
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Water seeping into fashionable running shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainers are sports shoes worn for running.

clue.text: Possibly flags errors

blocks.note: first meaning: flags are irises, which are plants that flower
second meaning: blunders, in informal British usage

explanation.walkthrough: 'flags' suggests banners, but it is the iris, a flowering plant; 'Possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are things that bloom, and also informal British slang for embarrassing mistakes.

clue.text: Less interesting, Brenda Lee's first hit

indicators.note: the opening letter of the preceding word is taken
letters that are struck are knocked about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the initial letter of Lee

explanation.surface: A dismissive review of Brenda Lee's first chart hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' reads as a hit record by the singer Brenda Lee, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Blander is the comparative of bland, meaning duller or less interesting.

clue.text: Prince with king and English wife

blocks.note: with and and both mean together
R is short for Rex, Latin for king
E is the abbreviation for English
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A prince appears with the king and his English wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Andrew is a son of Queen Elizabeth II, a royal prince.

clue.text: Wayne exhausted and unsmiling in this?

definitions.text: Wayne exhausted and unsmiling in this?

indicators.note: an exhausted thing is emptied out, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: Wayne with its insides emptied out
a stern face is unsmiling

explanation.surface: John Wayne, worn out and grim-faced in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the actor John Wayne was usually weary and stern-faced in this kind of film.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a cowboy film, the genre John Wayne is famous for.

clue.text: Son affected by first taste of iffy seafood

indicators.note: a first taste is only the beginning, so just the opening letter is used

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
camp means affected or exaggerated in manner
the initial letter of iffy

explanation.surface: A son taken ill after a first taste of dodgy seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustine tails, usually fried in breadcrumbs, a seafood dish.

clue.text: Wine overturned: it's the last drop of Cava

indicators.note: the last drop of something is its final bit, so its end letter is kept
turned over means the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of Cava

explanation.surface: A glass of wine is knocked over, spilling the last drop of fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: Cava is Spanish sparkling wine, which makes 'Wine' at the start look like part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: Steps up where batter is opening for Surrey

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so just the initial letter is used

blocks.note: in cricket a batter stands in the crease, a line marked by the stumps
the initial letter of Surrey

explanation.surface: A batter steps up to open the innings for Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county cricket team; 'opening' suggests an opening batter, but it selects a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up output is to raise it, so increases is a synonym.

clue.text: Hum song and dance

blocks.note: first meaning: a bad smell
second meaning: a fuss or commotion

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all music, but hum is British slang for a smell and a song and dance is a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A stink is both a foul odour and a public row, as in kicking up a stink.

clue.text: That lady unwrapped new present

new without its first and last letters

explanation.definitionFit: Someone present is here, in this place.

clue.text: See some revolutionary types, eco-idealists

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters running from the end of types into eco-idealists

explanation.surface: Watch a few radical green campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a bishop's see.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the area under a bishop's authority, which is a diocese.

clue.text: Very big piece on board needing kind of weak glue

size is a thin glue used to seal paper or plaster

explanation.definitionFit: Man-size means large, big enough for an adult man.

clue.text: Unpleasant imp splutters milk in churns

indicators.note: churning stirs things up violently, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'churns' looks like the noun for milk containers, but it is a verb signalling the anagram.
